text:
raj: Quick heads-up from the night profiler run — saw a weird tail latency bump on the CUDA hosts when cache-hit ratio climbed past ~65%. p50 stayed flat but p95->p99 jumped by ~120ms on long prompts. suspect the batcher is overpacking because it treats KV-cache hits as full tokens.

olivia: Hmm that matches a dev dogfood run I saw. Are you seeing increases in token budget overshoot or just packing inefficiency?

raj: Overshoot. The batch formation logic uses 'effective_length = requested_tokens' and then applies target_token_budget=2048. But when prefix is cache-hit we should use kv_cache_saved_tokens to reduce effective length. Example from trace: request had prompt 400 tokens, 380 of which were prefetched from KV; batcher counted full 400 and put it into batch causing larger per-step kernel runs.

sam: Do you have the trace snippet? even a summed counter will help. Also kernel selection may be picking larger workspace kernels because reported seq_len was high. That could explain the p99 spike.

raj: Paste of condensed trace: ```
// trace id 0x7f22
request_id: r-19
reported_seq_len: 1024
kv_cache_hit_tokens: 380
requested_gen_tokens: 64
batcher_effective_len_used: 1024
kernel_chosen: gpt_attn_fp16_tile128
// result: p99 add 120ms vs baseline
```

ana: (cc @olivia) I ran an A/B on a small fleet: baseline batcher vs patch that subtracts kv_cache_hit_tokens from effective_length. Results: baseline p99 310ms, patched p99 185ms, p50 identical. throughput slight +3%. sample size ~12k requests.

olivia: Nice. Is there any counterexample where subtracting cached tokens causes underpacking (too many small batches) and increases overhead?

ana: We saw very slight increase in kernel launch count (+2%) but amortized work was much lower, so net latency win. Edge case: requests with tiny uncovered suffix (e.g., 4 tokens) got batched with long sequences and caused more small-kernel kernel choices. I added a floor clamp: effective_length = max(min_len_floor, requested_tokens - kv_cache_hit_tokens) where min_len_floor=8.

sam: Can we do this conservatively in admission control instead of packing? Maybe track two metrics: effective_tokens_for_packing and profiling_tokens_for_kernel_selection. Kernel selection may still need to see original full sequence length for certain fused ops.

raj: Good point. My quick diff applied the subtract only for packing size calculation, not for kernel selection. Patch snippet: ```diff
- effective_len = requested_tokens
+ effective_len_for_packing = max(min_floor, requested_tokens - kv_cache_hit_tokens)
+ effective_len_for_kernel = reported_seq_len
```

olivia: Sounds right. Also we should update the batching simulator to model cache-hit-aware packing. I can add a mode flag. If we don't simulate, rollouts will surprise us.

perf-bot: perf/regression check completed: PR #3412 baseline -> kv-aware-pack shows no subjective regression on 10k synthetic cases. p95 improved 18%, p99 improved 40%. CI note: two kernel autotune jobs increased compile time by ~30s.

raj: Good. One more nuance: quantized kernels sometimes use different workspace heuristics and they keyed off reported_seq_len too. I think we should keep kernel selection grounded on reported_seq_len but provide an override to prefer smaller kernels when the majority of tokens are cached. I sketched a policy: if kv_cache_hit_ratio >= 0.6 and uncovered_tokens <= 64 -> prefer low-latency kernel.

sam: That heuristic seems fine but let's ensure we record telemetry: per-request kv_cache_hit_ratio, effective_len_for_packing, kernel_chosen, and kernel_latency. Add to the per-route dashboard.

ana: Agreed. I've got a small job running across dedicated pool with the clamp + kernel preference. Early numbers look consistent with the sim. After the run I'll post the compare table.

olivia: Next steps: (1) add kv-aware packing mode to simulator + unit tests, (2) land the packing-only change behind feature flag, (3) run canary on 10% of traffic on a subset of regions, (4) monitor p99 and kernel-selection telemetry for 24h.

raj: I'll open the RFC and link the sim results + trace samples. Thanks all. :raised_hands:

sam: FYI, file ticket for kernel autotuner to consider kv-hit profile as an input dimension. Might avoid repeated compile churn. :memo:

perf-bot: CI note: artifacts uploaded to perf-artifacts/2001234567/kv-aware-pack/ for deeper inspection.
